p: The Holbeck address puts you in the old industrial heart of south Leeds, an area once lined with flax mills and engineering works. It's handy for the M621 and the M62, so families from Wakefield, Bradford and beyond can be here in no time.

Since Roundhay and the Royal Armouries are already on your radar, here are a few more ideas. Leeds Industrial Museum at Armley Mills, just up the road, is housed in what was once a huge woollen mill and has working machinery, old steam engines and a cinema from yesteryear. Further along the Aire, Kirkstall Abbey is a spectacular ruined Cistercian abbey with free-to-roam grounds and plenty of space for kids to explore.

For a fun fact on your trip into the centre, Leeds Kirkgate Market is where Michael Marks opened his penny bazaar stall in 1884, the business that became Marks & Spencer. The market is still a brilliant, bustling spot for cheap eats and a nosy round the stalls.
Steam fans can head south to the Middleton Railway, a heritage line in Hunslet with engines, a museum and seasonal family events.

Practical bit: south Leeds traffic can be heavy at rush hour and on Leeds United match days at nearby Elland Road, so pick your time wisely and you'll breeze in and out. After that, the rest of the day is yours.

If you've got a whole weekend, split it in two: active stuff like the trampolines and the abbey grounds on day one, then museums and the market on day two. That way nobody's legs give up halfway through and everyone gets a bit of what they fancy.
